patch_description: The metrics plateau at 0.62 across many filter tweaks: lag_error stuck at 0.41, responsiveness at 0.71, while noise metrics barely move. The bottleneck is the structural phase/group delay of the SG + convolution pipeline, not the post-hoc snapping. A principled fix is predictive lag compensation: after smoothing, extrapolate the local quadratic trend forward by roughly the effective group delay (half the SG window + half the convolution window ≈ window_size samples). This is a classic zero-phase-lag technique (equivalent to "smoothed prediction" / forward-stepping the SG polynomial fit). It directly targets lag_error and responsiveness without adding noise, since extrapolation uses the already-denoised, curvature-aware quadratic fit rather than raw data. Compute the slope (first difference) and half-acceleration (second difference) of x_smooth via vectorized gradients, then step y forward: y_pred = y + delay*(dy + 0.5*delay*d2y). Clip the correction by the local noise sigma to avoid over-shooting in flat noisy regions (safety cap), preserving reversal performance. This is O(n), adds negligible execution time, and leaves all proven snapping machinery intact.
